body.statement: For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\), conditional on proving \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), the observed joint-bridge functional \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable if and only if \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever this holds, every gradient lies in \(\mathcal A_P\) and \[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2],\qquad V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].\] The claim is not unconditional: the projection becomes the canonical gradient only after the reverse score-lifting inclusion is established.
body.justification: Conditional on the explicit reverse-inclusion obligation, this identifies the regularity frontier and global canonical gradient across all bridge pairs in the simultaneous-existence observed-law model.
body.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already supplies root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity; BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified supplies regular selected-pair inference. Neither result proves the complete tangent and normal geometry or the global affine-hull bound when both bridge-existence restrictions define the observed model.
body.consumer: Analysts with redundant proxies can distinguish a valid selected-pair standard error from the global joint-model information bound.
